evals.prompt: Install TypeScript globally so I can run tsc in this repository. The repository already has pnpm-lock.yaml.
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes one-bin because a global install was requested, avoids the unnecessary global installation, uses the repository's pnpm owner, and proposes a project-local dependency or pnpm exec route.

evals.prompt: Install ripgrep for the whole machine and make sure every terminal uses it.
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes one-bin, audits existing rg candidates, chooses declarative Nix in dotfiles, validates a Darwin build, refreshes a shell, and verifies the selected real path without creating npm or Bun globals.

evals.prompt: I installed the same CLI with npm, Bun, and Nix, but command -v still points to npm. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes one-bin audit exe, identifies every owner in PATH order, verifies the Nix replacement before asking to remove obsolete npm and Bun owners, refreshes the shell, and confirms one canonical target.

evals.prompt: Add a dependency to this new personal TypeScript project. It has package.json but no lockfile or packageManager field.
evals.expected_output: The agent follows the baseline dependency policy without reading one-bin/SKILL.md or running its audits, confirms the project is genuinely new and personal, defaults to Bun, and creates only bun.lock.

evals.prompt: Put this direct-download macOS app under Homebrew management without losing its data.
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes one-bin, reads the macOS application and removal references, audits current provenance and ownership, does not force Homebrew adoption, presents a deliberate one-owner migration with data preservation and App Management checks, and requires approval and a verified recovery plan before removal.

evals.prompt: Add zod to this existing repository. It declares npm@10.9.2 in packageManager and has package-lock.json.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the declared npm workflow to add a project-local dependency and update only package-lock.json, without reading one-bin/SKILL.md, running one-bin audits, or introducing Bun or pnpm lockfiles.

evals.prompt: Update an existing dependency and refresh pnpm-lock.yaml in this pnpm repository.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the repository's declared pnpm version and normal update and validation workflow, without loading one-bin or treating the lockfile update as a manager migration.

evals.prompt: Add httpx to this Python project. It uses uv, pyproject.toml, and uv.lock.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the project's uv environment and lockfile without loading one-bin, installing globally, or modifying an agent runtime environment.

evals.prompt: Deliberately migrate this npm repository to Bun, including its lockfile, packageManager declaration, and CI install commands.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads one-bin and the project-manager migration reference, confirms the target owner, updates declarations and CI consistently, regenerates the Bun lockfile, retires the npm lockfile intentionally, performs a clean install, reviews resolution changes, and validates the project without removing machine-wide npm.

evals.prompt: Add a dependency in this directory. It has package.json but no lockfile or packageManager field; I have not said whether it is new or personal.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks repository instructions and asks for the missing ownership context before choosing a manager; it does not infer a Bun default or load the machine-wide one-bin workflow for this routine dependency request.

evals.prompt: Upgrade this machine-wide CLI. Its executable resolves into /nix/store, but it offers a built-in self-update command.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads one-bin and the machine-wide reference, audits executable ownership, updates the declarative Nix configuration rather than using the self-updater, validates and activates through the documented dotfiles workflow, and verifies the command in a fresh shell.

evals.prompt: My normal terminal says command not found for a machine-wide CLI I used yesterday. Install another copy so it works again.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads one-bin, audits the executable and manager inventories, inspects shell PATH and resolution before assuming absence, and repairs the verified owner's exposure instead of blindly creating another global installation.

evals.prompt: Remove this old machine-wide database runtime. I do not know whether anything still uses it or where its data lives.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads one-bin and removal safety, identifies the owner, dependents, running services, and data locations, and obtains explicit approval plus a verified recovery plan before removing the runtime or its data.
